correctness.rationale: For a,c,alpha>0 with q=alpha*a and y=x sqrt(a/c), the exact min cap/Polyak rule is F_q(y)=(1-q)y on q<=1/2+1/y² and F_q(y)=y/2-1/y otherwise; formulas agree at the boundary. For 0<q<2, capped steps strictly reduce |y| and once capped remain so; the uncapped condition forces y²>1/(q-1/2)>2/3, on which |y/2-1/y|<|y|. A hypothetical perpetually uncapped orbit would have a nonzero magnitude limit satisfying |r/2-1/r|=r, hence r²=2/3, contradicting the branch lower bound. Therefore every orbit eventually caps and geometrically converges (zero is absorbing). For q>=2, y*=sqrt(2/3) has proposal exactly 2 and F_q(y*)=-y*, producing a persistent 2-cycle; f=c/3, δ=4c/3*(1-1/q) by direct substitution. Independently tested normalized cycle at q=2,2.5,10; verifier.py checks additional representative cases but analytic argument handles all q.
